faq.question: Does OpenRouter use your data?
faq.answerHtml: OpenRouter processes your prompts and sends them to the selected model provider, but it doesn’t store prompt or response content by default. It records request metadata and may anonymously categorize a small sample. Full logging and product-improvement data sharing are optional.

faq.question: Is OpenRouter safe for sensitive data?
faq.answerHtml: Yes, OpenRouter can be safe for sensitive data if configured correctly. Turn off prompt logging and data sharing, choose zero-retention endpoints, and remove unnecessary information from requests. Teams with strict compliance or data residency requirements should check enterprise terms or add an extra governance layer.

faq.question: Is OpenRouter a legitimate company?
faq.answerHtml: Yes. OpenRouter is a legitimate company founded in 2023 and backed by established investors. In August 2026, Stripe agreed to acquire it. Some public reviews report problems with billing, support, and account security, but those concerns are separate from the company's legitimacy.

faq.question: What is OpenRouter used for?
faq.answerHtml: OpenRouter gives developers unified API access to hundreds of text, image, audio, and other multimodal AI models. Common uses include experimenting with different models, application development, provider comparison, cost-based routing, and automatic fallback.

faq.question: How does OpenRouter work?
faq.answerHtml: You can connect to OpenRouter through its Python or Node.js SDK or interact with the REST API directly. Your application sends a request to the OpenRouter API and specifies a model or routing preference. OpenRouter selects an eligible provider, forwards the prompt, receives the output, and returns it in a standardized format. The request cost is then deducted from your credit balance.

faq.question: Which is better, OpenRouter or OpenAI?
faq.answerHtml: OpenRouter acts as an AI gateway, providing access to multiple models through a single API. OpenAI is a model developer and direct API provider offering its own GPT and reasoning models. The right choice depends on whether you value easy setup and multi-model flexibility or a direct relationship with the provider.

Because Langdock cost depends heavily on how many users and how much usage you expect, the best approach is to request a tailored quote and model the cost against your projected usage rather than comparing headline prices alone.

faq.question: How do I migrate from Langdock to another platform?

Evaluate two or three alternatives in parallel, plan your access controls and SSO in advance, and cut over department by department rather than all at once. This staged approach keeps disruption low and lets you confirm each team is set up before the next moves.

eu-ai-act.description: Understand the EU AI Act: what it is, its risk tiers, updated 2026–2028 deadlines, fines, latest news, and what US and global teams should do to prepare.
intro: The EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive law governing artificial intelligence, and its reach extends well past Europe's borders. It applies extraterritorially, so US and global companies whose AI outputs reach people in the EU fall inside its scope.

Its obligations are rolling out in phases through 2028. A 2026 package of amendments (the Digital Omnibus on AI) shifted several key dates, which makes following EU AI Act news and knowing the current timeline more important than ever. This article is an informational overview of the EU AI Act, not legal advice. For decisions about your specific situation, consult qualified counsel.

faq.question: Has the EU AI Act been passed?
faq.answerHtml: Yes, the EU AI Act has been passed. It was formally adopted as Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 and entered into force on 1 August 2024. Its provisions apply in stages rather than all at once, and a 2026 amendment package (the Digital Omnibus on AI) adjusted several of the later application dates, which is why EU AI Act latest news today still matters even though the law itself is settled.

faq.question: Is the EU AI Act mandatory?
faq.answerHtml: Yes, the EU AI Act is mandatory and legally binding across all EU member states. Organizations that fall within its scope must comply, and non-compliance can lead to fines of up to $35M or 7% of global annual turnover for the most serious incidents, with a lower ceiling applied to SMEs and startups.

faq.question: What is an EU AI Act summary in one sentence?
faq.answerHtml: An EU AI Act summary in one sentence: the EU AI Act is the world's first comprehensive AI law, using a four-tier, risk-based system to regulate AI in the EU, with obligations rolling out in phases through 2028 and reaching any company, EU-based or not, whose AI reaches people in the EU.

ai-governance.description: Learn what AI governance is, the frameworks and best practices behind it, and how to build a program that keeps AI use safe, compliant, and accountable.
intro: AI governance is how you keep control of your AI: the policies and oversight that make sure every system you deploy stays safe, compliant, and accountable, instead of drifting somewhere you never intended. Most organizations are rolling out AI faster than they can keep a handle on it, and when a model produces a biased outcome or an expensive mistake, few can point to who owns it.

This guide covers what AI governance actually is, the principles behind it, and the frameworks and tools that support it. We’ll also lay out the exact steps to build a program that keeps your use of AI safe, compliant, and accountable. By the end, you'll know how to put AI governance into practice instead of leaving it on a slide.

faq.question: What is an example of AI governance?
faq.answerHtml: A clear example of AI governance is assigning a named owner to a hiring model, running a bias risk assessment before launch, logging every AI-driven decision it makes, and setting an independent escalation path for complaints. That combination of ownership, review, and audit trails is AI governance in action, and it's what practical AI governance looks like day to day.

faq.question: What is an AI governance framework?
faq.answerHtml: An AI governance framework is a structured set of policies, roles, and controls that guides how you develop, deploy, and monitor AI across its lifecycle. Frameworks like the NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 give you a reusable blueprint so you don't have to build effective AI governance from scratch. A robust AI governance framework scales as your AI systems and AI use grow.

faq.question: Who is responsible for AI governance?
faq.answerHtml: Responsibility for AI governance is shared, but it must be specific. An executive sponsor is accountable for AI risk overall, a governance lead owns policy and escalation, and a system owner is accountable for each AI system, with legal and security supporting throughout. Collective responsibility only works when every AI system also has one named owner.

faq.question: How do you measure AI governance effectiveness?
faq.answerHtml: You measure AI governance effectiveness with concrete signals: the share of AI systems with a named owner, the completeness of your AI inventory, the number of risk assessments completed, incident response times, and audit-trail coverage. Track these over time, and you can show that your AI governance is improving, not just documented.
